official.application_route: Secure admission to an eligible Irish HEI first, then submit one application with proof of admission and two references through the GOI-IES online portal linked from the HEA page; no applications by email, post or telephone.
official.citizenship_residency: Domiciliary of origin outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the United Kingdom; Russian and Belarusian citizens are not eligible. United Kingdom citizens are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: The scholarship is only for international students: applicants must have a domiciliary of origin outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK. Asylum seekers and refugees may apply if they meet all other criteria, and there is no age limit.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Scholarships are awarded across all disciplines, subject to the availability of places. It is the host institutions that decide for which courses they will provide fee waivers, so applicants must confirm course eligibility directly with the institution.
official.duration: One year of full-time, in-person study at NFQ level 9 or 10 (master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD). Scholarships are not extended beyond one academic year, although host institutions may extend the fee waiver for three-semester courses at their discretion.
official.description: The HEA describes the programme as supporting high-calibre international students who wish to study at NFQ levels 9 or 10 (master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD) in Ireland. It is funded by the Government of Ireland in partnership with Irish higher education institutions and managed by the Higher Education Authority, with 60 scholarships awarded each year for one year of full-time study.
official.program_type: National government scholarship for international postgraduate study at NFQ levels 9 and 10, delivered in partnership with Irish higher education institutions and managed by the Higher Education Authority
official.english_requirement: The HEA states that applying for the GOI-IES does not require an English language proficiency certificate, although institutions may request one for admission. All application materials and references must be in English, with notarised translations acceptable.

applicant_utility.summary: This is Ireland's flagship national scholarship for non-EU postgraduate students: a EUR 10,000 stipend for one year plus a full fee waiver from the host institution, with 60 awards made each year. You cannot apply for the scholarship alone: admission to an eligible Irish institution must be secured first, so the real pressure point is the course-admission timeline months earlier, not the March call itself. Competition is intense and scoring favours the personal statement (45 marks) over academic record (40 marks), so a well-argued case for studying in Ireland matters more than a perfect transcript. Note that the HEA itself frames the stipend as a contribution to living costs, not a full living allowance.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU applicants who can secure a taught master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD offer from an eligible Irish institution well before the March call and can articulate specific, long-term links with Ireland.
application_readiness_checklist: Start course applications to eligible Irish institutions 6-12 months ahead of the expected late-January call opening, so a conditional offer is in hand before the 12 March deadline
Email the GOI-IES contact for your chosen institution (Appendix 1 of the call document) to confirm your specific course accepts GOI-IES scholars before applying

Brief two referees early: references must be 500-700 words, written in English, signed by hand or electronically (a typed name is not accepted), dated within a year of the deadline, and uploaded by you through the portal

Draft the personal statement directly against the published marking scheme: benefit to you, the institution, Ireland and your country of origin; planned involvement in Irish society; long-term links with Ireland

Save the offer letter, admissions-office email or applicant-portal screenshot for the 2026/27 year as your proof of admission, and re-check every field before submitting because nothing can be edited afterwards
common_rejection_risks: No offer in hand at the deadline: the HEA will not accept an application without proof of admission, and an offer arriving after 12 March cannot be added
Answering a preliminary eligibility question incorrectly: the portal's automated check blocks ineligible candidates, and the portal allows at most two submissions including failed ones
Vague or generic personal statements and references, which the call document warns will score lower
Third-party drafted or AI-generated application content, which is prohibited and can invalidate the application
Submitting more than one eligible application or opening multiple accounts, which is treated as fraud and disqualifies all applications
Failing an institutional cut: some institutions prioritise holders of final offers over conditional ones during shortlisting
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to Ireland, study materials, health insurance and most daily living costs: the call document states the EUR 10,000 is a contribution to living costs and 'unlikely to cover them completely', and the FAQs confirm no travel or study-materials funding. You must also fund the first weeks in Ireland yourself, since the first EUR 5,000 instalment only arrives towards the end of October, plus the institution's application fee, which is not waived under the scheme.
document_audit: Offer documents must explicitly be for 2026/27; an offer letter, an admissions-office email, or a portal screenshot all qualify, but only one offer may be submitted per application
If you deferred entry to 2026/27, attach the institution's deferral confirmation; if already studying there, attach its confirmation that you will continue in 2026/27
References need an official header (or a brief explanation of its absence), the referee's organisational postal address and email, and no familial, financial or close personal relationship with you
If final grades are not yet available, state the grades achieved so far and the period covered, for example 5 semesters out of 6
alerts: The 2026 call closed at 5pm Irish time on 12 March 2026: applications cannot be submitted after the deadline and no alterations can be made once submitted
No feedback is given to unsuccessful applicants, the HEA's decision is final, and there are no post-completion requirements such as returning to your home country
Scholars must live in Ireland for the duration of the scholarship and commence in September or October; blended courses qualify only if all in-person classes are attended in Ireland
Awards cannot be transferred to another course or institution, and a conditional offer that is not met rescinds the award
2027 dates were not published when checked, so watch the HEA GOI-IES page from late 2026 for the next call
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create an account on the GOI-IES online portal, pass the automated eligibility check, then complete and submit the single application with the offer document and two references well before the 5pm Irish-time deadline.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a modest one-off cut to first-year tuition rather than a funding package: EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 off your year-one non-EU fee bill depending on your region, with nothing towards rent, flights or living costs. The application is deliberately light, an online form with your school results and a short statement about contributing to Trinity life, so the effort should go into submitting quickly rather than polishing for weeks. Awards are made on a rolling basis with hard regional closing dates, and the exempt-programme list quietly removes several of Trinity's most applied-to degrees.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Strong non-EU school leavers holding a year-one offer in a non-exempt discipline who want a partial fee break and can complete the short online form promptly after their offer arrives.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your course is not exempt (medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, computer science and statistics) before investing effort
If you are applying from China, redirect to the Claddagh Undergraduate Scholarship instead of this scheme
Check that your fee status is billed at the non-EU rate, since EU-fee-status students do not qualify
Have clear transcripts or certified translations of your secondary / high school results ready to reference in the form
Submit as soon as your offer arrives rather than waiting for your regional closing date, since assessment is rolling
common_rejection_risks: Applying for an exempt programme, where the award simply does not apply regardless of results
Missing the region-specific final date: the Americas (1 April) and Africa (1 May) close months before the July date that applies to South East Asia and Oceania
Assuming renewal: the award covers year one only, so later years need separate funding
Hearing nothing and not realising silence means unsuccessful, since Trinity does not contact unsuccessful applicants individually
Failing to fully accept the course offer, which forfeits the award
A generic contribution statement that could sit on any university application, which weakens the community-contribution criterion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Everything beyond year one: the award is a one-off EUR 2,000-5,000 reduction of first-year tuition, leaving the balance of the non-EU tuition fee for year one and the full cost of subsequent years, flights, accommodation and living expenses to be funded privately or through other awards.
document_audit: Only three inputs are requested: personal details, secondary / high school results and the community-contribution statement, so a course offer and school transcript are the only supporting materials you realistically need
The contribution statement is the only real differentiator, so name specific societies, clubs, volunteering or cultural activities you would join rather than praising Trinity in general terms
If the online form is blocked in your country, contact your Trinity Regional Manager / Advisor early for the alternative application form instead of waiting until the deadline
Keep evidence of your offer and its acceptance, since awardees must fully accept the offer to receive the award
alerts: All 2026/27 regional deadlines had passed when checked and the 2027/28 timetable was not published; the listed regional months (April to July) are the best guide to when the next round will open
Successful applicants are contacted shortly after their regional closing date; if no communication arrives within that window, assume the application was unsuccessful
The award is applied to your tuition fee bill rather than paid to you as cash, so it cannot be used for rent, flights or living costs

Exempt-programme students are pointed to school-level scholarships instead, so check the E3 education scholarships page if you hold an offer in engineering, natural sciences or computer science and statistics
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the online form (or the advisor-issued alternative) with your offer details, school results and contribution statement; Trinity then assesses region by region on a rolling basis and applies any award to your tuition fee bill once you fully accept your offer.
